question: Does pointing at a folder find the footage in it, and never the files SIEVE put there itself?

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2025-02-06-git-6da82b4485-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers

notes: footage is generated: a handful of tiny clips encoded on the spot, so detection is checked against a folder this file made rather than whatever is in video-tests/
detect: '3 sources · under a second · 64×48 · 1 skipped' from a folder also holding two text files and a truncated one
derived: 3 sources before and after its own output appeared, in the default location and in one named nothing special
exclude: exports/ excluded, 3 sources, and the document remembers
identity: a folder moved on disk is one row, under the id in its own document
library: 2 rows, newest first, an unmounted folder kept and marked, forgetting a row leaving the folder alone
carry: an unchanged folder costs a stat per file, and only what changed is opened again
adopt (a document, and one identity): 2 checked, 0 disagreed
detect (video, and nothing else): 3 checked, 0 disagreed
derived (never its own output): 3 checked, 0 disagreed
library (a list, not a filesystem): 3 checked, 0 disagreed
